news.title: World Cup: FIFA chief Gianni Infantino offers £30m incentive for members to back controversial private investment plans
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has given football associations until September 19 to back his plan to sell off part of FIFA to private investors - with a $40m (£30.1m) incentive to accept, a letter has revealed. FIFA announced on Tuesday that it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments. Under the proposal, FIFA would raise up to $4.2bn (£3.1bn) from external investors through the sale of minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it says would be valued at around $20bn (£15bn). The governing body says its plans - which need approval from member associations - could deliver more than $10bn in "football development funding" over the next four years.

news.title: Galatasaray manager defends Leroy Sané after World Cup disaster
news.lede: It has been over a month since Germany crashed out of the World Cup in (a not so) spectacular fashion. Julian Nagelsmann was criticized for his erratic decisions with the team, setup, tactics, and everything in between. One of the primary points of contention was sticking with Leroy Sané despite the winger underperforming massively. Okan Buruk, Sané’s manager at Galatasaray, found it amusing that his player is being labeled as the poster boy for Germany’s disappointing campaign.

news.title: Outrage over FIFA’s attempt to sell off the World Cup
news.lede: FIFA is at the centre of football’s latest storm. The idea of selling stakes in its flagship tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cups and the Club World Cup, to private investors has triggered a fierce backlash in which president Gianni Infantino has emerged as the main target. “Football is not for sale”, “None of us owns football. It is not for FIFA to sell it” and “Once you have sold a part, you have sold yourself” are among the phrases now echoing across the game.
